description: Somos un equipo de Santiago del Estero apasionado por la tecnología, la exploración espacial y la innovación. Para el desafío CLPS Lunar Mission Browser buscamos desarrollar una experiencia web interactiva, visual y fácil de explorar, combinando programación, diseño y visualización de datos. Nuestro objetivo es transformar información sobre misiones lunares en una experiencia atractiva, intuitiva y educativa.
summary: LUMOX addresses a specific question: if a lunar landing at the Moon's south pole is delayed, which sites and dates remain viable, and how much margin is available? Using real ephemerides from SPICE and JPL Horizons, together with actual LOLA terrain data, it calculates Sun and Earth visibility, available energy, and communication conditions on an hourly basis. Results are expressed as delay margins in days, required mast heights in meters, and potential relocation distances in kilometers. It includes a first-person view of the lunar terrain, featuring craters named according to IAU and USGS nomenclature. The platform offers three modes: Outreach, Operations, and Science. Every calculation can be traced step by step. Each data point identifies its source, and illustrative elements are clearly labeled.
details:
What does it do?

LUMOX simulates Sun–Earth–Moon geometry for a selected location. It calculates the local horizon using the LOLA digital elevation model, the visible fraction of the solar and Earth disks, the longest period of darkness, communication outages, and the energy balance. Its assessment is based on these metrics.

What makes it different?

It includes a landing delay margin panel showing how far the arrival date can shift; a first-person 3D viewer with an adjustable mast height ranging from 2 to 10 meters; and a complete trace of every calculation, including its formulas, inputs, and outputs.

How did we verify it?

We compared SPICE against JPL Horizons, obtaining maximum azimuth differences of 5.4 × 10⁻⁷°. We also implemented 24 automated tests.

Limitations

Performance at 60 FPS has not yet been verified on physical hardware. The coordinates of several locations, including Blue Ghost, Chandrayaan-3, and Malapert, have not been independently cross-checked. A comparison with QuickMap has also not been completed, as it requires human review. Terrain textures are visual elements only and are not used in the calculations.

Technologies

Python (FastAPI, NumPy, spiceypy, pyproj, rasterio, and pyshp), React, Vite, and Three.js.
